To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Inception V3 classifier can be retrained for accurate detection of pathogens in NGS based metagenomic data.
we have retrained a CNN (‘Inception V3’) to classify pathogenic bacteria at the species/strain level using metagenomic Ngs-reads.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of deep learning to detect microbes in metagenomic images and is a step towards developing a computational framework for the detection of multiple objects in metagenomic data.
the development of an efficient computational method to detect multiple pathogens in a single image (genomic data), which can be used for the precise characterization of microbial communities.

the development of an efficient, accurate and cost-effective computational method to classify pathogens at species and strain levels, and the development of a metagenomic NLP-based classifier for the simultaneous detection of multiple microbes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed method is an accurate, fast, and inexpensive method of classifying microbes in a metagenomics image.
the retrained ‘Inception V2’ classifier can accurately classify Campylobacter spp. and E. coli strains with 100% validation accuracy and 96% test accuracy.

the proposed approach is a fast and accurate computational approach to classify microbes at species level, using metagenomic data, which could potentially be used for pathogen detection and characterization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a computational method that uses NGS-reads as an image and CNNs as a classifier for the accurate detection and classification of pathogenic microbes.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of using NGS-data for accurate classification of microbes by harnessing the power of CNNs.

the retraining of ‘Inception-V3’ classifier with metagenomic images of microbes resulted in an efficient and accurate classifier, which could be used as an alternative to the existing classification methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a retraining of a pre-trained CNN classifier can be a fast and accurate way to classify microbes in a metagenome.

the retrained ‘Inception V2’ can be used to classify microbes at species/strain-level with a very high accuracy, and that this classifier can be trained on a small scale (50 images/class) and is robust to noise.
a simple retraining of a CNN classifier can be used to classify microbes from NGS-data.
